```
1	v0.17.0 — gate verifiability: tagging success criteria with who can verify them
2	
3	## Motivation — and a warning against the obvious reading
4	
5	The proximate trigger for this proposal is milestone M0 of the reigh-app
6	state-management refactor (`~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ideas/M0-render-telemetry.txt`).
7	Codex, running autonomously in a Railway container, shipped the actual code
8	deliverables — hook, overlay, 11 instrumented components, branch
9	`megaplan/m0-render-telemetry` — and then review blocked `done` with four
10	failures: a spec required "≥5 components × ≥3 interactions" of *observed*
11	render counts (needs a browser); a spec required a "non-HMR production-built
12	dev server" baseline (Vite strips `import.meta.env.DEV`, making the spec
13	semantically self-contradictory); `npm test` had 4 order-dependent failures
14	(real, but not caused by the milestone); and the baseline doc's directory
15	was `.gitignore`'d so codex force-added it (flagged as scope creep).
16	
17	The obvious reading is "add a `verified_by: human` tag so the reviewer
18	skips those criteria in autonomous mode." That reading is too shallow and
19	this proposal will resist it. Three deeper frames matter more:
20	
21	1. **The harness conflates plan gates with review gates.** The list of
22	   bullets under `## Gate criteria (for the human reviewer)` in the M0
23	   spec was written for a human reading a PR, and then reused verbatim
24	   as the review criteria. Megaplan has no concept that a spec may carry
25	   two audiences. The container runs with the human-facing list and is
26	   then punished for being unable to satisfy it.
27	2. **Spec authorship has no feedback loop.** Nothing in megaplan looks
28	   at a spec before execution and asks "are these criteria reachable by
29	   the agent configured to execute this plan?" The author pastes
30	   best-practice gates from CLAUDE.md; megaplan dutifully hands them to
31	   review; review dutifully fails. The error is diagnosed at the most
32	   expensive possible moment — after a full execute pass in a remote
33	   container.
34	3. **The review agent already has a `waived` escape hatch and doesn't
35	   use it aggressively.** `megaplan/prompts/review.py:503` instructs
36	   review to mark criteria `waived` "if a criterion cannot be verified
37	   in this context (e.g., requires manual testing or runtime
38	   observation)". In the M0 run this path was not taken — the reviewer
39	   treated "cannot verify interaction counts" as a `must` failure rather
40	   than a waiver. So the mechanism exists but the contract is ambiguous:
41	   unverifiable versus failed is a judgement call, with no structural
42	   signal from the spec telling the reviewer which one applies.
43	
44	Any proposal that only addresses frame 1 will succeed on M0 and then
45	fail on the next poorly-authored spec. A proposal that addresses all
46	three is a real fix.
47	
48	## Option space
49	
50	### (a) Per-criterion `verified_by: container|human|mixed` tag
51	Reviewer skips (waives) any criterion tagged `human` when running in an
52	autonomous context. Small change: schema plus two lines of reviewer
53	logic. Catches: obvious human-only gates. Misses: the authorship problem
54	(author has to remember to tag; no enforcement), the dual-audience
55	problem (still one criteria list), the expensive-machine-gate problem
56	(e2e suites are neither human nor container-easy). Low implementation
57	cost; zero worker-contract change; fully backward compatible (missing
58	tag = `container` default).
59	
60	### (b) Plan-phase verifiability audit
61	Before critique starts, the harness runs a lightweight check — most
62	cheaply a single worker call — that inspects each proposed success
63	criterion and emits a flag if the criterion is unreachable by the
64	configured worker. Catches: bad authorship early, when it is cheap to
65	fix. Misses: criteria that look machine-verifiable but aren't (dev-only
66	telemetry, flaky e2e). Medium cost; requires a new prompt and a new
67	flag category; plays well with the existing critique→gate loop because
68	the flags become part of normal resolution. Does not require a schema
69	change if we keep it advisory.
70	
71	### (c) Deferred-verification terminal state
72	Add a plan state `awaiting_human_verification` distinct from `done`.
73	Human-tagged criteria short-circuit the review `needs_rework` verdict
74	and instead park the plan in this state; a human CLI command
75	(`megaplan verify-human --plan X --criterion C --pass`) flips it to
76	`done`. Catches: the end-to-end lifecycle including "who actually
77	confirmed". Misses: still requires the tagging from (a) upstream; adds
78	a new state machine branch that has to be taught to status, batch
79	runners, and loop-init. Medium-to-large cost; meaningful worker
80	contract change (review must emit a new verdict `awaiting_human` in
81	addition to `approved` / `needs_rework`).
82	
83	### (d) Two-array schema split (machine_criteria, human_criteria)
84	The plan author writes two explicit arrays. Review evaluates only
85	`machine_criteria`. `human_criteria` go into the PR description or a
86	checklist file and never touch review. Catches: the conflation directly
87	at the schema level; makes the author's two audiences structurally
88	separate. Misses: authors who lazily shove everything into one bucket;
89	the expensive-machine-gate case. Small cost; but a large change in
90	authoring ergonomics — existing specs break unless we fall back to
91	treating `success_criteria` as `machine_criteria`.
92	
93	### (e) Reviewer self-assessment of verifiability
94	Let the reviewer return, per criterion, one of
95	`pass | fail | waived_unverifiable | waived_info`. Today's `waived`
96	covers both `info` priority and unverifiable; split that. The reviewer
97	decides, not the author. Catches: the M0 case without touching spec
98	authoring; the reviewer is usually in the best position to know what
99	it cannot verify. Misses: authors still paste nonsense criteria; the
100	loop wastes a whole execute pass before the reviewer shrugs; also
101	creates a new gaming vector where `waived_unverifiable` means "I didn't
102	try hard enough." Low cost in isolation.
103	
104	### (f) Worker capability profile + static criterion linter
105	New-for-this-proposal. Each worker declares a *capability profile* — a
106	small structured blob listing what it can execute (`run_shell`,
107	`run_node_tests`, `read_build_output`, `observe_browser`,
108	`observe_runtime_logs`, ...). At plan-finalize time, each success
109	criterion is parsed by a linter prompt that maps it to the capabilities
110	it needs. A criterion whose required capabilities are a subset of the
111	configured worker's profile is `machine_verifiable: true`. Everything
112	else is `machine_verifiable: false` and is automatically treated as a
113	human-deferred criterion. The author does not tag anything; the
114	harness computes it.
115	
116	## Recommendation: a fused (a)+(b)+(e), with (f) as the v0.18 follow-up
117	
118	Pick option (a) as the storage model, option (b) as the upstream defense,
119	and option (e) as the downstream safety net. Deliver all three in v0.17.0.
120	Defer (f) because capability profiles are a much bigger design problem —
121	they couple to worker contracts, the trusted-container env, and the
122	hermes worker, and we do not need them to fix the immediate pain. (c) is
123	tempting but adds a state machine branch for a problem that `waived`
124	already models well; reject. (d) forces existing specs to break; reject.
125	
126	Why fuse three rather than pick one: each option on its own has a
127	failure mode the other two cover.
128	
129	- (a) alone: author forgets to tag -> reviewer still fails. (e) catches.
130	- (b) alone: audit passes because criteria *look* machine-verifiable
131	  (e.g., "baseline counts captured" reads as machine-checkable but
132	  requires a browser). (a) plus (e) catch at review time.
133	- (e) alone: reviewer correctly waives, but the author never learns
134	  the spec was malformed; the next milestone repeats the mistake. (b)
135	  surfaces the problem at authorship.
136	
137	The three-layer structure mirrors megaplan's existing philosophy (plan
138	gate filters → execute audit → review verdict), just applied to the
139	verifiability axis.
140	
141	## Implementation sketch
142	
143	### Schema changes (`megaplan/schemas.py`)
144	`plan.json` and `finalize.json` success_criteria items gain:
145	```
146	"verified_by": {"type": "string", "enum": ["container", "human", "mixed"], "default": "container"}
147	"verification_hint": {"type": "string"}  // optional, free-text: "requires running browser", etc.
148	```
149	Review-output criteria gain a new `pass` enum value:
150	```
151	"pass": {"type": "string", "enum": ["pass", "fail", "waived", "waived_unverifiable", "deferred_human"]}
152	```
153	Existing `waived` is preserved for `info` priority. Missing `verified_by`
154	defaults to `container` — every existing plan keeps working unchanged.
155	
156	### Plan-phase audit (option b)
157	New file: `megaplan/verifiability.py`. Exposes `audit_criteria(state, criteria)`
158	which runs a single-shot worker call (same pattern as `run_gate_checks`)
159	asking: "for each criterion, is it reachable by a worker with capabilities
160	`run_shell`, `read_files`, `git`, but no browser, no human hands, no manual
161	observation? Return `container`, `human`, or `mixed` and one-line
162	rationale." Results are written to `plan_dir/verifiability.json` and
163	surfaced as advisory critique flags with category `verifiability`. The
164	author (or gate) can override by explicitly setting `verified_by` on the
165	criterion — the audit never overwrites an explicit tag, only fills in
166	missing ones.
167	
168	Runs after `finalize`, before `execute` starts. Keeps the
169	critique→gate→revise loop as the resolution surface — no new state.
170	
171	### Review-phase handling (option e)
172	`megaplan/prompts/review.py` gains two rules:
173	- If criterion's `verified_by == "human"`: reviewer MUST mark
174	  `pass: "deferred_human"` and MUST NOT count it toward the
175	  `needs_rework` tally. `review_verdict = approved` is valid even if
176	  every human criterion is deferred.
177	- If reviewer finds a `container`-tagged criterion it genuinely cannot
178	  verify (e.g., the tooling isn't present in this environment), it
179	  marks `pass: "waived_unverifiable"` with an evidence sentence naming
180	  *what* it couldn't run, and surfaces a flag `REVIEW-UNVERIFIABLE-NNN`.
181	  A `must` criterion going `waived_unverifiable` is a soft block — it
182	  downgrades verdict to `needs_rework` only if `>= N` of them occur
183	  (configurable; default 1 for `must`, infinity for `should`). This
184	  prevents the M0 cascade.
185	
186	Merging logic (`_merge_review_verdicts` at `handlers.py:1421`) must learn
187	the new enum values and stop treating them as `fail`.
188	
189	### CLI
190	- `megaplan audit-verifiability --plan X` — run the audit on demand.
191	- `megaplan status` shows counts: "3 container / 2 human / 0 mixed".
192	- `megaplan verify-human --plan X --criterion "Baseline doc captured"
193	  --pass --evidence "Confirmed 5 components × 3 interactions in doc
194	  at commit abc123"` — records the human confirmation in
195	  `plan_dir/human_verifications.json`. Review re-runs treat these as
196	  resolved. (Optional for v0.17.0; falls back to "human flips state
197	  with a comment" if we want to defer.)
198	
199	### Migration
200	- Existing plans without `verified_by`: default `container`. Same
201	  behavior as today.
202	- Existing plans in `awaiting_review` / `needs_rework` for the M0-class
203	  reason: add a one-shot retrofit script that parses the review verdict
204	  and re-tags criteria whose failure evidence includes phrases like
205	  "cannot verify", "no browser", "requires manual". Offered as a CLI
206	  tool, not automatic.
207	- Tests: add fixtures under `tests/fixtures/verifiability/` that mirror
208	  M0 — container-only execution, spec with mixed gates, expected
209	  `approved` verdict with deferrals.
210	
211	### Out of scope (v0.17.0)
212	- Worker capability profiles (option f). Deferred to v0.18.0 when we
213	  re-examine worker contracts wholesale.
214	- Schema-level split into two arrays (option d). Tag is sufficient.
215	- Auto-flipping `awaiting_human_verification` based on PR comments or
216	  GitHub checks. Manual CLI confirmation only.
217	- Teaching loop mode about deferrals. v0.17.0 treats a plan with any
218	  `deferred_human` criteria as "done for autonomous purposes"; loops
219	  continue to the next plan.
220	
221	## Success criteria (verifiable)
222	
223	- `megaplan init` accepts plans whose `success_criteria[].verified_by`
224	  is `container`, `human`, or `mixed`. Missing field defaults to
225	  `container` — asserted by schema round-trip test.
226	- `megaplan audit-verifiability --plan X` produces
227	  `verifiability.json` with one entry per criterion and exits 0.
228	- A fixture plan with a `verified_by: human` criterion runs through
229	  review and yields `review_verdict: approved`, `pass: deferred_human`
230	  for that criterion, and no `rework_items` entries sourced from it.
231	- A fixture plan with an undetectable-by-container criterion (e.g.,
232	  "browser renders without warnings") and `verified_by` unset triggers
233	  a verifiability flag at audit time, category `verifiability`.
234	- Reviewer emitting `pass: waived_unverifiable` on a `must` criterion
235	  still routes to `needs_rework` (soft block preserved); emitting it
236	  on a `should` criterion does not.
237	- `megaplan verify-human --plan X --criterion C --pass --evidence E`
238	  writes `human_verifications.json` and, on a re-review, the entry is
239	  honored: verdict stays `approved`, pass flips from `deferred_human`
240	  to `pass`.
241	- Existing test suite passes unchanged — all legacy plans default to
242	  `container` and behave exactly as before.
243	- `pyproject.toml` version is `0.17.0`; CHANGELOG has the v0.17.0 entry.
244	
245	## Edge cases — and answers
246	
247	- **Mixed human + machine gates in one plan.** Supported first-class;
248	  review emits both `pass` and `deferred_human` verdicts; `approved` is
249	  possible when all machine `must` criteria pass and all human `must`
250	  criteria are deferred. The plan status becomes `approved_with_deferrals`
251	  in `status` output — a label, not a new state.
252	- **Worker identity changes mid-plan** (claude plans, codex executes,
253	  hermes reviews). Capability is conservatively the intersection across
254	  the executing + reviewing workers. The audit runs with the *executor's*
255	  profile; review with its own. If review has fewer capabilities than
256	  execute, `waived_unverifiable` can still fire at review time — this is
257	  correct: review couldn't verify, regardless of whether execute could.
258	- **Machine-verifiable but expensive** (full e2e, 30-minute build).
259	  These are `verified_by: container` but get a `verification_hint` of
260	  `"expensive"`. Not handled in v0.17.0 — a future `verified_by: container_slow`
261	  tag would let the harness choose to defer them in CI-gated contexts.
262	  Explicitly out of scope now; the hint is present so we do not have to
263	  re-migrate schemas later.
264	- **Gaming: author marks everything `human` to skip checks.** Three
265	  defenses. (1) The verifiability audit runs regardless of the author's
266	  tag; if the audit says a criterion *is* container-reachable, that
267	  appears as a flag at gate time even when the author claimed `human`.
268	  (2) `megaplan status` surfaces the container/human ratio; a plan with
269	  7 human and 0 container criteria is visually anomalous to the human
270	  operator. (3) Review's `waived_unverifiable` counter still applies —
271	  marking something `human` does not exempt it from the soft block if
272	  review independently finds the claim is machine-checkable. We do not
273	  try to make gaming impossible; we make it visible.
274	
275	## Authorship ergonomics
276	
277	Today a spec author writes one list of bullets. Under v0.17.0 they write
278	the same list, and most criteria default to `container` implicitly. The
279	only new burden is tagging the criteria they already know a machine
280	cannot verify. To lower even that burden:
281	
282	- The `megaplan init` prompt gains a one-line nudge: "Any success
283	  criterion that requires human observation (browser, device, QA
284	  confirmation) should set `verified_by: human`."
285	- A scaffolding command `megaplan new-spec --template milestone` writes
286	  a template markdown file with two example criteria pre-filled, one
287	  per `verified_by` value, so the author sees the shape.
288	- The verifiability audit's output is itself the teaching signal: if
289	  the author forgets, the flag surfaces with rationale and the author
290	  learns the pattern on the next spec.
291	
292	The system is strictly *easier* to get right: the failure mode goes
293	from "ship to a container, burn a run, fail review opaquely" to
294	"critique emits a flag at plan time, author adjusts tag or rewrites
295	criterion." The only way v0.17.0 is harder than today is if the author
296	wants to preserve the current behavior of pasting CLAUDE.md bullets
297	into the criteria block — which is exactly the behavior we are trying
298	to make uncomfortable.
299	
300	## Branch
301	`gate-verifiability` off main.

4	## Verdict
5	
6	The proposal is directionally right and operationally wrong. It correctly
7	identifies that M0 failed not because Codex was incompetent but because the
8	spec contained gate criteria that no container agent could ever satisfy, and
9	it correctly refuses the shallow "just add a tag" reading. But the fused
10	(a)+(b)+(e) solution is a three-subsystem compromise that partially solves
11	each of the three frames without fully solving any, adds a new terminal-ish
12	label (`approved_with_deferrals`) whose lifecycle is explicitly out of scope,
13	and introduces a `deferred_human` path that in the solo-operator model this
14	harness actually runs under will silently accumulate unchecked "done-ish"
15	plans. The real root cause is narrower than the proposal claims — it is a
16	missing *executor-capability contract*, not a missing author tag, missing
17	audit, and missing reviewer enum all at once. Option (f), which the proposal
18	explicitly defers, is the one that attacks the root; shipping (a)+(b)+(e)
19	first mortgages schema surface area against a v0.18 that will then have to
20	re-migrate. Ship a scoped revision — keep (b) as the centerpiece, collapse
21	(a) into advisory-only, drop (e)'s new enum values, delete `deferred_human`

31	the system fails loudly: review returns `needs_rework` and the plan parks.

223	      # verdict ∈ {machine_verifiable, unverifiable_needs_rewrite,
224	      #            unverifiable_human_only}
225	  ```
226	
227	  Results become first-class critique flags (category:
228	  `verifiability`, severity: blocking if `unverifiable_needs_rewrite`,
229	  noted if `unverifiable_human_only`). The existing gate → revise
230	  loop resolves them: the author either rewrites the criterion to be

236	  no `approved_with_deferrals` label. A plan either has machine-verifiable
237	  criteria (passes review) or it doesn't (fails review, as today).
238	
239	This is ~150 LOC: one new file (`verifiability.py`), one hook in
240	`handlers._run_critique`, one new flag category in `prompts/critique.py`,
241	and tests. It attacks frame 2 (authorship feedback) directly, which is
242	the frame with the largest M0-class payoff. It does not attack frames 1
243	and 3 — but frames 1 and 3 are mostly downstream consequences of frame
244	2 going unaddressed.

247	
248	- Each worker declares a capability blob in `megaplan/workers.py`:
249	  ```python
250	  @dataclass
251	  class WorkerCapabilities:
252	      can_run_shell: bool
253	      can_read_build_output: bool
254	      can_observe_browser: bool
255	      can_observe_runtime_logs: bool
256	      can_run_tests: bool
257	      ...
258	  ```
259	- The verifiability audit from v0.17.0 is upgraded: instead of a
260	  free-form natural-language "is this reachable", it emits a set of
261	  required capabilities per criterion and the harness does a pure-Python
262	  set-subset check against the executor's declared profile. Ground
263	  truth, no prompt-drift.
264	- Review uses the same profile: a criterion whose required caps are
265	  not a subset of the *reviewer's* caps is automatically `waived`
266	  with a concrete "reviewer lacks cap X" evidence string. No new enum.
267	- Mid-plan worker swap becomes principled: the harness computes the
268	  intersection at finalize time and surfaces it in `plan.json`'s
269	  meta.
270	
271	This is the real fix. Deferring it to v0.18 is fine — the v0.17.0
272	audit is small enough that re-plumbing it when v0.18 lands is ~1 day
273	of work, and meanwhile the advisory-only prompt-based audit catches
274	the easy M0-class cases at authorship time, which is the highest-ROI
275	slice.

## Executive summary (200 words)

Capability matching is directionally better than both v0.17.0 and the critique's audit-only path, but the "one concept replaces three subsystems" pitch is partly rhetorical — it shifts complexity rather than eliminating it. Eight concrete losses vs. alternatives, four of them load-bearing:

1. **Capability vocabulary has no registry/owner** — becomes a tagging treadmill with typos routing silently; needs a closed enum plus style rules forbidding criterion-shaped capabilities.
2. **Plan-time hard failure kills exploratory "ship code anyway" mode** that v0.16/v0.17 preserve; needs `--allow-unverifiable` escape hatch.
3. **Pending-human queue is the silent-accumulator concern renamed**; needs `status --pending-human`, loop-driver warnings, and single clearing path.
4. **Grain-size mismatch** — capabilities are coarse, criteria fine; `requires ⊆ verifies` is necessary not sufficient.
5. **Composite requirements** can't be expressed as flat sets; the exact M0 failure (HMR-stripped `import.meta.env.DEV`) still slips through.
6. **Worker discovery is unspecified**; the solo-dev guarantee depends on it.
7. **Gaming moved not solved** — `requires: []` is the new `verified_by: human`.
8. **Default `requires: []` gives existing plans zero benefit** for a month.

Recommendation: ship v0.18.0 capability matching WITH the critique's pre-critique audit preserved, plus four specific modifications (closed registry, audit retention, explicit worker discovery, mandatory `requires` on `must`). Do not ship as drafted; do not ship audit-only.

set -euo pipefail

> DEVELOPER

You are the autonomous megaplan runner for this single run.

Project: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan
Idea: Add a `megaplan tiebreaker` command that takes an architectural/design decision question and produces structured context for a human final call, by running two subagents in sequence (researcher → challenger) and presenting their output in a decision-ready format.

## Full spec the run should implement

**Motivation.** When megaplan's `gate` returns ESCALATE because the plan's constraints are inconsistent (needs a human architectural decision), the human is left with just the gate rationale. No structured research, no stress-test. A `megaplan tiebreaker` subcommand can call two 125-IQ-engineer-style subagents with different mandates, then output their findings in a shape that makes the final call fast and well-informed.

**Reuse, don't reinvent.** The researcher is a stripped-down plan-phase worker with a research-focused prompt. The challenger is a stripped-down critique-phase worker that reads the researcher's output. Both write to artifact files next to the plan's other artifacts. Reuse the worker dispatch machinery (run_codex_step / run_claude_step / SessionDB) — do NOT reinvent.

**CLI shape.**
```
megaplan tiebreaker --plan <name> --question "..." [--output tiebreaker.md]
megaplan tiebreaker --plan <name> --question-file path/to/decision.md
megaplan tiebreaker status --plan <name>
```

The question file or inline question states the decision, the constraints that can't all hold, and any pinned context (relevant files, patterns to consider).

**Phase flow inside the subcommand (not new top-level phases):**

1. **Researcher pass** — worker reads the question, the repo, the plan's current state (if any), and the critique history. Produces `tiebreaker_researcher.json` with fields:
   - `question`: echoed
   - `evidence`: array of `{claim, evidence_type: "code|measurement|pattern|doc", file_paths: [...], quote: "..."}`. Facts, not opinions.
   - `options`: array of `{name, description, assumptions, costs}`.
   - `preliminary_pick`: `{option_name, rationale, what_I'm_least_sure_about}`.

2. **Challenger pass** — second worker, fresh session, reads the researcher's JSON plus the question and repo. Produces `tiebreaker_challenger.json`:
   - `measurements_vs_assumptions`: array of `{researcher_claim, classification: "measured|assumed|unsupported", note}`.
   - `missing_options`: array of `{name, description, why_it_was_missed}`.
   - `hard_cases`: for the researcher's pick, array of `{scenario, why_it_breaks_or_forces_workaround}`.
   - `reframings`: array of `{alternative_framing, which_original_constraint_it_drops, tradeoff}`.
   - `aging_analysis`: `{option_name, year_out_regret_scenario}` per option.
   - `counter_recommendation`: `{option_name | "confirm_researcher", rationale}`.

3. **Synthesis output** — final `tiebreaker.md` (or the configured --output path) structured for the human reader:
   ```
   # Decision: <question>
   
   ## Options considered
   (table: option | researcher cost | challenger risk | aging risk)
   
   ## Evidence summary
   (bullet list of measurements + where assumptions hide)
   
   ## Researcher pick vs challenger call
   (side-by-side)
   
   ## Where they agree (strong signals)
   ## Where they disagree (taste zones)
   
   ## Recommended framing
   (the strongest single framing the run produced, not an auto-pick)
   
   ## Fallback plan
   (what to do if the picked option looks wrong in 2 weeks)
   ```

**Important design rules:**
- Two separate persistent sessions for researcher and challenger; challenger must NOT see researcher's session, only the JSON output. Independence is the point.
- Both workers use codex by default (config `agents.tiebreaker_researcher` and `agents.tiebreaker_challenger`, defaulting to codex). Claude is a valid alternative and should be configurable.
- Researcher's prompt explicitly asks for evidence-over-opinion; challenger's prompt explicitly asks for stress-test-not-restate.
- Tiebreaker does NOT auto-resolve the original plan's state. It's advisory. Human runs it, reads the output, then decides whether to `force-proceed`, `add-note`, `replan`, or abort the parent plan.
- `megaplan tiebreaker status` shows whether researcher, challenger, and synthesis have each completed.
- Idempotent: re-running writes new artifacts with v2/v3 suffixes, doesn't overwrite.
- Testable: unit tests for prompt rendering, JSON schema validation of researcher/challenger output, synthesis markdown rendering.

**Out of scope for this milestone:**
- Auto-resolving the parent plan (no automatic force-proceed). The output is advisory.
- More than two agents (no third "verifier"). Keep to researcher + challenger.
- Multi-question batching (one question per run).
- Graphical output, web UI, anything beyond markdown + JSON artifacts.
- Tiebreaker-specific session management beyond what SessionDB already supports.

**Files likely to change:**
- NEW: `megaplan/tiebreaker.py` (orchestrator).
- NEW: `megaplan/prompts/tiebreaker_researcher.py`, `megaplan/prompts/tiebreaker_challenger.py`, `megaplan/prompts/tiebreaker_synthesis.py`.
- NEW: `schemas/tiebreaker_researcher.json`, `schemas/tiebreaker_challenger.json`.
- MODIFIED: `megaplan/cli.py` (new `build_tiebreaker_parser` + dispatch).
- MODIFIED: `megaplan/handlers.py` (new `handle_tiebreaker`).
- MODIFIED: `megaplan/types.py` (new TypedDicts if needed).
- MODIFIED: `pyproject.toml` (version → 0.17.0 if this lands before the verifiability work; otherwise coordinate — read current version and bump appropriately).
- MODIFIED: `CHANGELOG.md`.
- NEW: `tests/test_tiebreaker.py`.

**Branch:** `tiebreaker-subcommand` off `main`.

## Execution meta
Execution mode: auto-approve (raw_config.execution.auto_approve=true — do NOT add --auto-approve flag)
Robustness: light (user explicitly requested)

Launcher: `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan` for every CLI call.

## Startup
1. cd /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan
2. Run: `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan init --project-dir /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan --robustness light "<paste the full spec above as the idea text>"`
3. Capture the plan name. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line.
4. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.

## Loop (light)
`init -> plan -> critique -> revise -> finalize -> execute -> done`. No prep, gate, or review.

## After every phase
Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`. Trust CLI state over memory.

## Breakpoints (rare)
Only PHASE_ESCALATE (phase fails twice — once normal + once --fresh) or EXECUTE_ESCALATE (3 consecutive no-progress execute attempts). Format:
`BREAKPOINT: <type>`
`Plan: <name>`
`State: <state>`
`Summary: <reason>`
`Context: <details>`

## Completion
`COMPLETE: megaplan run finished`
`Plan: <name>`
`Final state: <state>`
`Summary: <outcome>`
`Artifacts: <key files / PR URL>`
`Follow-up: <only if needed>`

Version coordination: another subagent is concurrently working on v0.17.0 verifiability contracts. Check `pyproject.toml`'s current version. If it's 0.14.4 (unchanged), bump to 0.17.0 for this work. If it's already 0.17.0, bump to 0.17.1 and note in CHANGELOG that tiebreaker ships alongside verifiability contracts. If unclear, add a note to the PR body flagging the coordination.

Begin now.

> DEVELOPER

You are the autonomous megaplan runner for this single run.

Project: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan
Idea: Add automated tiebreaker triggering + guardrails to megaplan. Builds on the `megaplan tiebreaker` CLI command being built in a concurrent light-megaplan run (branch `tiebreaker-subcommand`). This run adds the second layer: gate-driven automatic triggering, state machine extension, and all the guardrails. This is the v2 of tiebreaker — MVP was "human manually invokes tiebreaker"; v2 is "harness detects recurrence and routes to tiebreaker automatically with budgeted, audited guardrails."

## Full spec

**Motivation.** Today, gates can only recommend PROCEED / ITERATE / ESCALATE. When a plan has an unresolvable constraint tension (like M1's RQ-first vs store-first architectural conflict), the only path is ESCALATE — but the human gets only the gate's rationale, no structured decision context. The MVP tiebreaker CLI produces that context manually. This milestone makes the harness recognize when tiebreaker should run and route automatically — with enough guardrails that it doesn't burn tokens on false positives.

**Core changes**

### 1. Iteration-pressure signal (compute in evaluation.py / gate_signals.py)

For each open flag, compute:
```
{flag_id, fuzzy_group_id, iterations_open, addressed_then_reopened_count, rationale_similarity_to_prior}
```

`fuzzy_group_id` is assigned by embedding similarity on the flag's `concern` text — flags with >0.85 cosine similarity belong to the same fuzzy_group. This catches "bootstrap race" flags labeled with different IDs across iterations but semantically the same concern. Use a small local embedding model (or an API call if that's already how critique works); make the similarity threshold configurable.

`addressed_then_reopened_count` counts transitions: flag went from `open` to `addressed` and back to `open`. That's the strongest signal of loop failure.

This table is rendered into the gate prompt context as a plain-text section.

### 2. Extend gate schema and prompt

`megaplan/schemas.py`:
```python
GATE_RECOMMENDATION = Literal["PROCEED", "ITERATE", "ESCALATE", "TIEBREAKER"]

class GateOutput(TypedDict):
    recommendation: GATE_RECOMMENDATION
    rationale: str
    flag_resolutions: list[FlagResolution]
    tiebreaker_question: NotRequired[str]   # required iff recommendation == TIEBREAKER
    tiebreaker_flag_ids: NotRequired[list[str]]  # which flags this resolves
    tiebreaker_fuzzy_group_id: NotRequired[str]  # which group this resolves
```

`megaplan/prompts/gate.py` gets a new section:
> "If any fuzzy_group shows `addressed_then_reopened_count ≥ 2` OR has ≥2 member flags across ≥2 iterations, consider whether it reflects an *unresolvable constraint tension* (architectural/philosophical — requires a human call → TIEBREAKER) versus a *plan-quality issue* (the plan writer hasn't tried hard enough → ITERATE). Recommend TIEBREAKER only for the former; cite specific flag IDs and iterations in your rationale."

### 3. Harness validates TIEBREAKER recommendation

In `handlers.py` `handle_gate`:
- If gate returns `recommendation: TIEBREAKER`, check that at least one fuzzy_group has `addressed_then_reopened_count ≥ 2` OR spans ≥2 iterations.
- If no such group exists, reject the recommendation and re-prompt the gate once with: "You recommended TIEBREAKER but no flag shows mechanical recurrence signal. Either identify specific flag(s) with iteration history or pick ITERATE."
- If re-prompt still says TIEBREAKER without signal, force-demote to ITERATE and log `tiebreaker_rejected_no_signal`.

### 4. New plan states

`megaplan/types.py`:
```python
PlanState = Literal[
    ..., "critiqued", "gated", "finalized", "executed", "reviewed", "done",
    "tiebreaker_pending",  # NEW — tiebreaker recommended, researcher/challenger running
    "tiebreaker_ready",    # NEW — synthesis done, awaiting human decision
]
```

Transitions:
- `critiqued` → (gate emits TIEBREAKER, validation passes) → `tiebreaker_pending`
- `tiebreaker_pending` → (tiebreaker runs) → `tiebreaker_ready`
- `tiebreaker_ready` → (human runs `megaplan tiebreaker decide`) → `critiqued` (with settled flag resolution injected)

### 5. New CLI: `megaplan tiebreaker decide`

```
megaplan tiebreaker decide --plan <name> --pick <option_name> --rationale "..."
megaplan tiebreaker decide --plan <name> --escalate --rationale "..."  # human chooses to handle outside the tool
megaplan tiebreaker decide --plan <name> --replan --rationale "..."    # question itself is wrong
```

Implementation:
- Write decision to the plan's `flag_registry` as `settled_by_tiebreaker` against the `fuzzy_group_id`.
- Record the decision in `tiebreaker_decisions.json` with full context (researcher pick, challenger pick, human pick, rationale, timestamp).
- Transition state back to `critiqued`. Next revise inherits the settled resolution.

### 6. Settled-decision immunity in critique prompt

In `megaplan/prompts/critique.py`, add a section listing settled_by_tiebreaker decisions for the current plan. Prompt instruction:
> "The following concerns have been settled by human tiebreaker decision. Do NOT re-raise them under a new surface. Only raise a new concern if new evidence *materially* changes the settled premise — and if so, explicitly cite which settled decision you are challenging and why."

### 7. Guardrails

- **Budget per plan.** `plan_config.max_tiebreakers_per_plan` (default 2). Counted in the plan's state metadata. Exceeded → gate's TIEBREAKER force-demoted to ESCALATE with rationale `"tiebreaker budget exhausted"`.
- **Cost ceiling.** Tiebreaker run has a wall-clock (default 30m) and token (default 150k) budget. Exceeded → abort, emit partial output, force-demote to ESCALATE.
- **Domain blocklist.** `plan_config.tiebreaker_blocklist: list[str]` (default `[]`). Concerns with category in blocklist skip tiebreaker.
- **Spec-level opt-out.** Idea file front-matter field `allow_tiebreaker: false` disables the entire mechanism for the plan.
- **Tiebreaker refusal.** Researcher can emit `decision_not_ripe: true` with reason; harness treats as abort without consuming a tiebreaker budget slot.

### 8. Audit tracking

`megaplan/audit.py` (new or extend existing):
- After each tiebreaker, record: `{plan_name, tiebreaker_index, fuzzy_group_id, question, researcher_pick, challenger_pick, human_pick, matched_researcher, matched_challenger, time_to_decide_seconds, tokens_spent, subsequent_plan_reached_done}`.
- New CLI: `megaplan tiebreaker audit [--plan X | --global]` — shows usage stats, hit rate, token cost. `--global` aggregates across all plans.

### 9. Tests

- Unit: `iteration_pressure` computes correctly across synthetic flag histories.
- Unit: gate schema validation rejects TIEBREAKER without `tiebreaker_question` + `tiebreaker_fuzzy_group_id`.
- Unit: `handle_gate` rejects TIEBREAKER without mechanical signal, re-prompts, force-demotes if re-prompt fails.
- Unit: budget enforcement (3rd tiebreaker recommendation on same plan demotes).
- Unit: settled-decision blocks critique from re-raising same fuzzy_group concern.
- Integration: synthetic plan with recurring flags runs through critique → gate → tiebreaker_pending → tiebreaker_ready → decide → critiqued with settled resolution.

### 10. Out of scope

- **Cross-plan tiebreaker detection.** Fuzzy-grouping is plan-local; cross-plan is v3.
- **Automatic tiebreaker resolution.** Human always decides — no auto-pick.
- **Tiebreaker on review phase.** This run does the gate path only. Review-phase tiebreaker is a follow-up.
- **Embedding model selection.** Use whatever critique already uses for text similarity. Don't introduce a new embedding dependency if one exists.
- **UI / TUI.** Markdown + JSON artifacts only.

### 11. Files

- NEW: `megaplan/tiebreaker_trigger.py` (gate signal + validation), or extend `gate_signals.py`
- NEW: `megaplan/audit.py` if it doesn't already exist, else extend
- MODIFIED: `megaplan/schemas.py`, `megaplan/types.py`, `megaplan/handlers.py`, `megaplan/cli.py`, `megaplan/prompts/gate.py`, `megaplan/prompts/critique.py`, `megaplan/evaluation.py`
- NEW tests in `tests/test_tiebreaker_trigger.py`

### 12. Version

Coordinate with concurrent runs. Read current `pyproject.toml` version:
- If 0.14.x unchanged → bump to 0.18.0 (leaving 0.15.0 doc-mode, 0.16.0 chain, 0.17.0 verifiability + tiebreaker CLI slots)
- If 0.17.x → bump to 0.18.0
- If 0.18.0 already → bump to 0.18.1 and note coordination in CHANGELOG
- If unclear, add a PR-body note flagging the version uncertainty.

Branch: `tiebreaker-auto-trigger` off main.

Extend gate schema and prompt\n\n\\`megaplan/schemas.py\\`:\n\\`\\`\\`python\nGATE_RECOMMENDATION = Literal['PROCEED', 'ITERATE', 'ESCALATE', 'TIEBREAKER']\n\nclass GateOutput(TypedDict):\n    recommendation: GATE_RECOMMENDATION\n    rationale: str\n    flag_resolutions: list[FlagResolution]\n    tiebreaker_question: NotRequired[str]   # required iff recommendation == TIEBREAKER\n    tiebreaker_flag_ids: NotRequired[list[str]]  # which flags this resolves\n    tiebreaker_fuzzy_group_id: NotRequired[str]  # which group this resolves\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n\\`megaplan/prompts/gate.py\\` gets a new section:\n> 'If any fuzzy_group shows \\`addressed_then_reopened_count >= 2\\` OR has >=2 member flags across >=2 iterations, consider whether it reflects an *unresolvable constraint tension* (architectural/philosophical — requires a human call -> TIEBREAKER) versus a *plan-quality issue* (the plan writer hasn't tried hard enough -> ITERATE). Recommend TIEBREAKER only for the former; cite specific flag IDs and iterations in your rationale.'\n\n### 3. Harness validates TIEBREAKER recommendation\n\nIn \\`handlers.py\\` \\`handle_gate\\`:\n- If gate returns \\`recommendation: TIEBREAKER\\`, check that at least one fuzzy_group has \\`addressed_then_reopened_count >= 2\\` OR spans >=2 iterations.\n- If no such group exists, reject the recommendation and re-prompt the gate once with: 'You recommended TIEBREAKER but no flag shows mechanical recurrence signal. Either identify specific flag(s) with iteration history or pick ITERATE.'\n- If re-prompt still says TIEBREAKER without signal, force-demote to ITERATE and log \\`tiebreaker_rejected_no_signal\\`.\n\n### 4. New plan states\n\n\\`megaplan/types.py\\`:\n\\`\\`\\`python\nPlanState = Literal[\n    ..., 'critiqued', 'gated', 'finalized', 'executed', 'reviewed', 'done',\n    'tiebreaker_pending',  # NEW — tiebreaker recommended, researcher/challenger running\n    'tiebreaker_ready',    # NEW — synthesis done, awaiting human decision\n]\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nTransitions:\n- \\`critiqued\\` -> (gate emits TIEBREAKER, validation passes) -> \\`tiebreaker_pending\\`\n- \\`tiebreaker_pending\\` -> (tiebreaker runs) -> \\`tiebreaker_ready\\`\n- \\`tiebreaker_ready\\` -> (human runs \\`megaplan tiebreaker decide\\`) -> \\`critiqued\\` (with settled flag resolution injected)\n\n### 5. New CLI: \\`megaplan tiebreaker decide\\`\n\n\\`\\`\\`\nmegaplan tiebreaker decide --plan <name> --pick <option_name> --rationale '...'\nmegaplan tiebreaker decide --plan <name> --escalate --rationale '...'  # human chooses to handle outside the tool\nmegaplan tiebreaker decide --plan <name> --replan --rationale '...'    # question itself is wrong\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nImplementation:\n- Write decision to the plan's \\`flag_registry\\` as \\`settled_by_tiebreaker\\` against the \\`fuzzy_group_id\\`.\n- Record the decision in \\`tiebreaker_decisions.json\\` with full context (researcher pick, challenger pick, human pick, rationale, timestamp).\n- Transition state back to \\`critiqued\\`. Next revise inherits the settled resolution.\n\n### 6. Settled-decision immunity in critique prompt\n\nIn \\`megaplan/prompts/critique.py\\`, add a section listing settled_by_tiebreaker decisions for the current plan. Prompt instruction:\n> 'The following concerns have been settled by human tiebreaker decision. Do NOT re-raise them under a new surface. Only raise a new concern if new evidence *materially* changes the settled premise — and if so, explicitly cite which settled decision you are challenging and why.'\n\n### 7. Guardrails\n\n- **Budget per plan.** \\`plan_config.max_tiebreakers_per_plan\\` (default 2). Counted in the plan's state metadata. Exceeded -> gate's TIEBREAKER force-demoted to ESCALATE with rationale 'tiebreaker budget exhausted'.\n- **Cost ceiling.** Tiebreaker run has a wall-clock (default 30m) and token (default 150k) budget. Exceeded -> abort, emit partial output, force-demote to ESCALATE.\n- **Domain blocklist.** \\`plan_config.tiebreaker_blocklist: list[str]\\` (default []). Concerns with category in blocklist skip tiebreaker.\n- **Spec-level opt-out.** Idea file front-matter field \\`allow_tiebreaker: false\\` disables the entire mechanism for the plan.\n- **Tiebreaker refusal.** Researcher can emit \\`decision_not_ripe: true\\` with reason; harness treats as abort without consuming a tiebreaker budget slot.\n\n### 8. Audit tracking\n\n\\`megaplan/audit.py\\` (new or extend existing):\n- After each tiebreaker, record: {plan_name, tiebreaker_index, fuzzy_group_id, question, researcher_pick, challenger_pick, human_pick, matched_researcher, matched_challenger, time_to_decide_seconds, tokens_spent, subsequent_plan_reached_done}.\n- New CLI: \\`megaplan tiebreaker audit [--plan X | --global]\\` — shows usage stats, hit rate, token cost. --global aggregates across all plans.\n\n### 9. Tests\n\n- Unit: iteration_pressure computes correctly across synthetic flag histories.\n- Unit: gate schema validation rejects TIEBREAKER without tiebreaker_question + tiebreaker_fuzzy_group_id.\n- Unit: handle_gate rejects TIEBREAKER without mechanical signal, re-prompts, force-demotes if re-prompt fails.\n- Unit: budget enforcement (3rd tiebreaker recommendation on same plan demotes).\n- Unit: settled-decision blocks critique from re-raising same fuzzy_group concern.\n- Integration: synthetic plan with recurring flags runs through critique -> gate -> tiebreaker_pending -> tiebreaker_ready -> decide -> critiqued with settled resolution.\n\n### 10. Out of scope\n\n- Cross-plan tiebreaker detection. Fuzzy-grouping is plan-local; cross-plan is v3.\n- Automatic tiebreaker resolution. Human always decides — no auto-pick.\n- Tiebreaker on review phase. This run does the gate path only. Review-phase tiebreaker is a follow-up.\n- Embedding model selection. Use whatever critique already uses for text similarity. Don't introduce a new embedding dependency if one exists.\n- UI / TUI. Markdown + JSON artifacts only.\n\n### 11. Files\n\n- NEW: megaplan/tiebreaker_trigger.py (gate signal + validation), or extend gate_signals.py\n- NEW: megaplan/audit.py if it doesn't already exist, else extend\n- MODIFIED: megaplan/schemas.py, megaplan/types.py, megaplan/handlers.py, megaplan/cli.py, megaplan/prompts/gate.py, megaplan/prompts/critique.py, megaplan/evaluation.py\n- NEW tests in tests/test_tiebreaker_trigger.py\n\n### 12. Version\n\nCoordinate with concurrent runs. Read current pyproject.toml version:\n- If 0.14.x unchanged -> bump to 0.18.0 (leaving 0.15.0 doc-mode, 0.16.0 chain, 0.17.0 verifiability + tiebreaker CLI slots)\n- If 0.17.x -> bump to 0.18.0\n- If 0.18.0 already -> bump to 0.18.1 and note coordination in CHANGELOG\n- If unclear, add a PR-body note flagging the version uncertainty.\n\nBranch: tiebreaker-auto-trigger off main.\n\nDependency note: the \\`megaplan tiebreaker\\` CLI (researcher + challenger + synthesis) is being built concurrently in branch tiebreaker-subcommand. This run's code depends on that CLI existing. If during plan phase you notice megaplan/tiebreaker.py is absent on main, note it in the plan's assumptions that this work assumes the subcommand exists via merge of tiebreaker-subcommand. You can still land this run's code on tiebreaker-auto-trigger — it will fail to exercise the CLI but tests can mock it. Surface the dependency clearly in the PR body.\"\n",

> DEVELOPER

You are running a multi-step operational workflow. Goal: get M1 unstuck on the Railway container by running the new `megaplan tiebreaker` CLI against M1's architectural tension, applying the verdict, and relaunching the chain.

## Context

- Plan `milestone-m1-from-docs-state-20260415-1011` on the container is stuck at state=`critiqued` with gate=ESCALATE. The loop iterated 4 times on the same architectural concern: how `createEntityStore` reconciles three constraints (lazy-load on first mount, RQ scaffolded externally, preserve current `useJoinClipsSettings` RQ behavior). These constraints are inconsistent.
- The `megaplan tiebreaker` CLI was just built in a concurrent subagent run (plan `add-a-megaplan-tiebreaker-20260415-1242`, state=done). The code is uncommitted on `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/` on main, mixed with uncommitted v0.17 verifiability contracts work.
- The container runs megaplan installed via `pip install git+https://github.com/peteromallet/megaplan.git@main`. It does NOT yet have the tiebreaker CLI.

## Steps

### 1. Push a temp branch with the combined uncommitted work

`cd /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan`. Current branch will be `chain-as-megaplan-command` or similar. `git status` to see everything uncommitted — expect changes across `megaplan/cli.py`, `handlers.py`, `types.py`, `schemas.py`, `capabilities.py` (NEW), `verifiability.py` (NEW), `tiebreaker.py` (NEW), `prompts/tiebreaker_*.py` (NEW), `_core/phase_runtime.py`, `prompts/{critique,planning,review}.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, plus tests.

- `git checkout -b tiebreaker-plus-verifiability-temp` (or similar name — it's a throwaway branch just to get the tiebreaker CLI onto the container)
- `git add -A`
- `git -c user.email=[REDACTED] -c user.name="POM" commit -m "TEMP: combined v0.17 verifiability + tiebreaker CLI for cloud M1 unblock — separate into two PRs later"`
- `git push -u origin tiebreaker-plus-verifiability-temp`

The intermixing is acknowledged technical debt — post-flight cleanup will separate into two proper PRs (`verifiability-contracts` and `tiebreaker-subcommand`). This temp branch is purely a vehicle to get the tiebreaker CLI onto the container.

### 2. Install the temp branch on the container

From `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev`:

```
railway ssh "pip install --force-reinstall --no-cache-dir --no-deps 'git+https://github.com/peteromallet/megaplan.git@tiebreaker-plus-verifiability-temp' 2>&1 | tail -3 && PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan tiebreaker --help 2>&1 | head -20"
```

Verify `megaplan tiebreaker --help` shows usage. If it doesn't exist, the tiebreaker CLI didn't land in the pushed branch — investigate before proceeding.

### 3. Run tiebreaker on the container against M1

The M1 question is architectural:

> **Question**: For `createEntityStore` in the reigh-app state management refactor (M1), how should it relate to React Query? The three stated constraints in the M1 spec can't all hold: (1) `useEntity(id)` lazy-loads authoritatively on first mount, (2) RQ-backed entities are scaffolded externally, (3) `useJoinClipsSettings` preserves current RQ behavior without a competing bootstrap path. Pick one of: (A) RQ-first — RQ owns fetching, store is a writeable mirror, factory drops the `load` parameter entirely, consumer bridges via `bootstrapEntity(id, data)` in a useEffect; (B) store-first — store's factory owns `load`, RQ wraps the store; (C) hybrid — per-entity declared ownership. Researcher should map actual RQ patterns in `/workspace/reigh-app/`, walk the exact race condition the critique worker kept catching, measure LOC cost of migrating `useAutoSaveSettings` consumers under each option, and produce a preliminary pick with what's most uncertain flagged. Challenger stress-tests, looks for missing options, identifies hard cases, and considers whether one of the three original constraints should be relaxed instead of picking an option.

Run on container:
```
railway ssh "cd /workspace/reigh-app && MEGAPLAN_TRUSTED_CONTAINER=1 mp-run tiebreaker-m1 bash -c 'cd /workspace/reigh-app && MEGAPLAN_TRUSTED_CONTAINER=1 megaplan tiebreaker --plan milestone-m1-from-docs-state-20260415-1011 --question \"<paste full question above>\" --output /workspace/m1-tiebreaker.md'"
```

Wait for completion (check via `railway ssh "tmux capture-pane -t tiebreaker-m1 -p | tail -20"` periodically, or `railway ssh "cat /workspace/m1-tiebreaker.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l"` until it's >0).

Expected wall time: 15-30 min (two codex sessions, research + stress-test).

### 4. Read the synthesis

When the markdown output exists, `railway ssh "cat /workspace/m1-tiebreaker.md"` and parse:
- Researcher's preliminary pick
- Challenger's counter or confirmation
- Agreement zones (strong signals)
- Disagreement zones (taste)
- Recommended framing

### 5. Make the human call

You are the human for this purpose. Read the synthesis, pick an option (A/B/C or a reframing), and write a decision rationale.

**Default pick if the synthesis is balanced:** Option A (RQ-first), because RQ is already the codebase's server-state authority. The M1 idea file's constraint #1 (lazy-load on first mount) is dropped as incorrect spec writing — the store should not own fetching. Factory signature drops `load`; `bootstrapEntity` is the only data entry point; consumer bridges RQ→store in `useEffect`.

**If the synthesis reveals a strong reason to override that default, override it.** Your job is to act on evidence, not stick to a default.

### 6. Apply the verdict to M1 via add-note

```
railway ssh "cd /workspace/reigh-app && megaplan override add-note --plan milestone-m1-from-docs-state-20260415-1011 --note '<verdict text>'"
```

The verdict text must:
- State the picked option clearly.
- Explain the architectural call in 2-3 sentences.
- Specify what drops (e.g., "constraint #1 dropped: store does not own fetching").
- Specify the concrete factory signature change (drop `load` param, `bootstrapEntity` is primary entry).
- Instruct the loop: "Settled by tiebreaker. Do not re-raise this concern under new surface. Revise the plan to reflect this architecture."

### 7. Relaunch M1 under supervisor

```
railway ssh "tmux kill-session -t exec 2>/dev/null; cd /workspace/reigh-app && MEGAPLAN_TRUSTED_CONTAINER=1 mp-run exec mp-supervise m1-post-tiebreaker bash -c 'cd /workspace/reigh-app && MEGAPLAN_TRUSTED_CONTAINER=1 megaplan auto --plan milestone-m1-from-docs-state-20260415-1011 --on-escalate fail --stall-threshold 5 --max-iterations 100 --phase-timeout 3600'"
```

### 8. Verify M1 is advancing

Wait 5-10 min, then check:
```
railway ssh "cd /workspace/reigh-app && megaplan status --plan milestone-m1-from-docs-state-20260415-1011 2>&1 | grep -E '\"state\"|next_step|phase_progress'"
```

State should have moved past `critiqued` (likely `planned` → `critiqued` → `gated` → `finalized` → `executed` over time) or the note should be visible in `notes` array. If it hasn't moved in 10 min despite supervisor being alive, surface the blocker.

## Constraints

- Do not force-proceed M1. The goal is to let the loop continue naturally with the settled decision injected as a note.
- Do not edit state.json. The override add-note command is the correct channel.
- Do not touch the uncommitted v0.17 or tiebreaker work on the Mac further — just push once to the temp branch in step 1, nothing else. Separating into proper PRs is a follow-up effort.
- The tiebreaker CLI was built in a concurrent run and may have rough edges. If it fails on the container (missing import, broken schema, etc.), debug minimally — fix the obvious bug in the temp branch, push, reinstall, retry. If it's fundamentally broken, fall back to: apply the default pick (Option A) directly via add-note without running tiebreaker, and note in the PR that tiebreaker CLI validation is still needed.
- Subscription billing on the container — do not trigger API-billed auth.

"""Tiebreaker subcommand — structured decision support for architectural questions.

Runs two independent subagents (researcher → challenger) then synthesizes
their output into a human-readable decision brief.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from megaplan._core import (
    atomic_write_json,
    atomic_write_text,
    read_json,
    resolve_plan_dir,
)
from megaplan.prompts.tiebreaker_challenger import challenger_prompt
from megaplan.prompts.tiebreaker_researcher import researcher_prompt
from megaplan.prompts.tiebreaker_synthesis import render_synthesis
from megaplan.types import CliError, PlanState
from megaplan.workers import run_step_with_worker


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version-suffix logic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _next_version_suffix(plan_dir: Path) -> str:
    """Scan for existing tiebreaker_researcher* artifacts and return the next suffix.

    First run → "", second → "_v2", third → "_v3", etc.
    """
    existing = sorted(plan_dir.glob("tiebreaker_researcher*.json"))
    count = len(existing)
    if count == 0:
        return ""
    return f"_v{count + 1}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Orchestrator
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _run_tiebreaker(
    root: Path,
    plan_dir: Path,
    state: PlanState,
    args: argparse.Namespace,
) -> int:
    question = _resolve_question(args)
    suffix = _next_version_suffix(plan_dir)

    researcher_file = f"tiebreaker_researcher{suffix}.json"
    challenger_file = f"tiebreaker_challenger{suffix}.json"
    synthesis_file = f"tiebreaker{suffix}.md"

    # -- Researcher pass --
    r_prompt = researcher_prompt(question, state, plan_dir, root=root)
    resolved = _build_resolved(args, "tiebreaker_researcher")

    researcher_result, r_agent, _, _ = run_step_with_worker(
        "tiebreaker_researcher",
        dict(state),  # FLAG-003: shallow copy to prevent state pollution
        plan_dir,
        args,
        root=root,
        resolved=resolved,
        prompt_override=r_prompt,
    )
    if not researcher_result.success:
        payload = {
            "success": False,
            "error": "researcher_failed",
            "message": researcher_result.error or "Researcher step failed",
        }
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
        return 1

    researcher_data = researcher_result.parsed or {}
    atomic_write_json(plan_dir / researcher_file, researcher_data)
    sys.stderr.write(f"[tiebreaker] researcher done → {researcher_file}\n")

    # -- Challenger pass --
    c_prompt = challenger_prompt(
        question, researcher_data, state, plan_dir, root=root
    )
    resolved_c = _build_resolved(args, "tiebreaker_challenger")

    challenger_result, c_agent, _, _ = run_step_with_worker(
        "tiebreaker_challenger",
        dict(state),  # FLAG-003: shallow copy
        plan_dir,
        args,
        root=root,
        resolved=resolved_c,

---SYNTHESIS---
# Tiebreaker: Decision Brief

## Decision

For `createEntityStore` in the reigh-app state management refactor (M1), how should it relate to React Query? The three stated constraints in the M1 spec can't all hold: (1) `useEntity(id)` lazy-loads authoritatively on first mount, (2) RQ-backed entities are scaffolded externally, (3) `useJoinClipsSettings` preserves current RQ behavior without a competing bootstrap path.

Pick one of:
(A) RQ-first — RQ owns fetching, store is a writeable mirror, factory drops the `load` parameter entirely, consumer bridges via `bootstrapEntity(id, data)` in a useEffect.
(B) store-first — store's factory owns `load`, RQ wraps the store.
(C) hybrid — per-entity declared ownership.

Researcher should map actual RQ patterns in `/workspace/reigh-app/`, walk the exact race condition the critique worker kept catching, measure LOC cost of migrating `useAutoSaveSettings` consumers under each option, and produce a preliminary pick with what's most uncertain flagged.

Challenger stress-tests, looks for missing options, identifies hard cases, and considers whether one of the three original constraints should be relaxed instead of picking an option.

## Options Considered

| Option | Description | Assumptions | Costs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A) RQ-first | React Query remains the fetch authority for settings. `createEntityStore` becomes a writable mirror only; consumers read `useToolSettings`, then bridge query results into the store with an effect such as `bootstrapEntity(id, data)`. | Settings entities should continue to follow the documented `server state = React Query` architecture.; Every RQ-backed consumer can safely maintain a second local mirror without introducing another authority problem.; Non-RQ entities can use a separate path, because dropping `load` removes the current custom-load/save capability from the factory itself. | This recreates the exact class of competing-bootstrap race already documented in `useShotSettings`, where local initialization must beat the RQ loader to avoid overwrite.; It expands migration work across the 13 current `useAutoSaveSettings` importers (2,129 LOC measured), because each migrated consumer needs its own query-to-store bridge.; It does not fit the existing production custom-load/save pattern in `useGenerationEditSettings` unless a second factory or parallel API is kept. |
| B) store-first | `createEntityStore` owns `load/save` for each entity; React Query becomes an implementation detail behind the store or wraps the store after the fact. | A Zustand store can become the canonical draft and hydration state for persisted settings without violating the app's server-state model.; The store can either call the same Supabase/settings primitives directly or await React Query-backed data without losing cache correctness.; The team is willing to shift away from the current documented layering where `useAutoSaveSettings` sits on top of `useToolSettings`. | This is an architectural reversal from the current docs: the repo explicitly says server state lives in React Query and has no Zustand today.; To preserve current behavior, the new store has to reproduce the existing settings state machine invariants now spread across `useAutoSaveSettings.ts` (609 LOC), `useDebouncedSettingsSave.ts` (274 LOC), `autoSaveSettingsLoaders.ts` (183 LOC), and `autoSaveSettingsHelpers.ts` (133 LOC).; Direct `useToolSettings` manual-control callsites still remain, so this does not eliminate the React Query boundary; it adds a second cross-cutting foundation unless more migration follows. |
| C) hybrid | Ownership is declared per entity/domain. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-owned; store-backed entities use store-owned `load/save`. The important rule is one authority per entity, not one authority for the whole app. | The codebase can tolerate two sanctioned ownership modes, because it already has both a React Query mode and a custom-load/save mode inside `useAutoSaveSettings`.; The M1 constraints must be relaxed for RQ-owned entities: if React Query is authoritative for a given entity, `useEntity(id)` cannot also be an authoritative loader for that same entity.; The main contract to preserve is single-authority hydration and save behavior, not that every entity must use the exact same bootstrap mechanism. | This requires an explicit ownership policy in code and docs so callers know whether an entity is RQ-owned or store-owned.; The factory API becomes more complex than a universal `load/save` contract, because some entities will not use internal `load` at all.; For M1 specifically, the team must accept that the original three constraints do not all hold simultaneously; at least the `useEntity(id)` authoritative-lazy-load rule has to be relaxed for RQ-backed settings like join-clips if RQ behavior is to remain unchanged. |
| D) Boundary-owned adapter, not consumer-owned bridge *(challenger)* | Keep React Query authoritative for settings, but do not make each consumer call `bootstrapEntity(id, data)` in an effect. Instead, put the bridge inside `useAutoSaveSettings` or a dedicated settings adapter so the RQ-to-store sync happens once at the boundary that already owns pending-edit and flush semantics. | — | — |
| E) Query-cache-as-store for RQ-backed entities *(challenger)* | For RQ-owned settings, `createEntityStore` does not hold a second canonical copy at all. It exposes selectors/actions over React Query cache plus a local draft buffer only while dirty. Persisted state stays in query cache; the store exists only for UI ergonomics. | — | — |
| F) M1 scope split: exclude RQ-backed settings from `createEntityStore` *(challenger)* | Declare that M1's factory is for entities without an existing RQ authority. Join-clips and other settings stay on `useAutoSaveSettings` for now; only custom-load/save entities or net-new state move to the factory. | — | — |
| G) Relax `useEntity(id)` into `ensureEntity(id)` + selector split *(challenger)* | Make loading explicit and separate from reading. `useEntity(id)` becomes a synchronous reader over whichever authority owns the data; `ensureEntity(id)` or route-level prefetch performs lazy authoritative loading. This removes the requirement that the same hook both read and authoritatively load. | — | — |

## Evidence Summary

- **The repository does not currently have a Zustand layer, and the documented frontend architecture still assigns server state to React Query.** [doc] (docs/structure_detail/frontend_architecture.md, package.json)
- **The settings stack is intentionally layered today: `useAutoSaveSettings` is the feature-level API, and `useToolSettings` is the low-level read/write boundary.** [doc] (docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md, src/shared/hooks/settings/useToolSettings.ts)
- **`useToolSettings` is explicitly a React Query boundary: it fetches with `useQuery`, writes with `useMutation`, and merges the mutation result back into the React Query cache.** [code] (src/shared/hooks/settings/useToolSettings.ts)
- **`useAutoSaveSettings` already has two distinct ownership modes: a React Query-backed mode and a custom `load/save` mode.** [code] (src/shared/settings/hooks/useAutoSaveSettings.ts, src/shared/settings/hooks/autoSaveSettingsLoaders.ts)
- **The current React Query loader has explicit guards to prevent query results from overwriting pending local edits, which means a second bootstrap path for the same entity is already treated as hazardous.** [code] (src/shared/settings/hooks/autoSaveSettingsLoaders.ts, src/shared/hooks/settings/__tests__/useAutoSaveSettings.test.ts)
- **A real competing-bootstrap race already exists in the codebase: `useShotSettings` relies on writing pending state before the React Query loader overwrites inherited defaults.** [code] (src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/settings/useShotSettings.ts)
- **The debounce/save state machine preserves newer edits during in-flight saves and flushes pending work on cleanup; any replacement store has to preserve those invariants.** [code] (src/shared/settings/hooks/useDebouncedSettingsSave.ts, src/shared/hooks/settings/__tests__/useAutoSaveSettings.test.ts)
- **`useJoinClipsSettings` is currently just a thin passthrough to `useAutoSaveSettings`, so its public contract is whatever `useAutoSaveSettings` returns.** [code] (src/tools/join-clips/hooks/useJoinClipsSettings.ts)
- **There is already one production consumer using `useAutoSaveSettings` in custom-load/save mode, which means the codebase already needs a non-React-Query path for some entities.** [code] (src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/useGenerationEditSettings.ts)
- **The migration surface is large if every current `useAutoSaveSettings` consumer must gain its own React Query bridge: there are 13 non-test importers totaling 2,129 LOC.** [measurement] (src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/useGenerationEditSettings.ts, src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/settings/useJoinSegmentsSettings.ts, src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/settings/useShotSettings.ts, src/tools/join-clips/hooks/useJoinClipsSettings.ts, src/tools/character-animate/hooks/useCharacterAnimateSettings.ts, src/tools/image-generation/hooks/useImageGenGallery.ts, src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/hooks/video/useStructureVideo.ts, src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/hooks/video/useAudio.ts, src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/hooks/video/useOutputSelection.ts, src/shared/settings/hooks/useEditVideoSettings.ts, src/shared/hooks/usePersistentToolState.ts, src/shared/components/PromptEditorModal/hooks/usePersistentPromptSettings.ts, src/shared/components/ImageGenerationForm/hooks/useShotManagement.ts)
- **Direct `useToolSettings` usage is smaller and concentrated in manual-control contexts, which aligns with the existing layering docs.** [measurement] (src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/useAddToVideoEditor.ts, src/shared/hooks/useHomeNavigation.ts, src/tools/video-editor/pages/VideoEditorPage.tsx, src/shared/contexts/AgentChatContext.tsx, src/shared/components/ToolsPane/ToolsPane.tsx)
